title: Standalone Vertex.clone() breaks the observation clone contract
counterpart: VertexView.clone() and actual runner observation facets
behavior: Vertex is structurally assignable to VertexView, whose clone promises an independent editable hint collection. Standalone Vertex.clone() reuses the original hint array; runner facets correctly copy it.
misuse: A function receiving VertexView pushes into view.clone().getChildrenHints() and unexpectedly changes a standalone input.
proposal: Make clone() copy the hint collection. If sharing is needed, expose cloneSharingHints() explicitly; keep data and individual hint payload identities shallow.
tradeoff: O(number of hints) copying; intentional shared-array clients change behavior. This finding concerns standalone substitution, not a mutable runner-handle leak.
fable: considered in owner appendix; not ranked

title: Walking limits patches silently replace existing budgets
counterpart: GraphWalkOptionsPatch versus field-wise inOrder and execution-selector patches
behavior: configure({ limits }) replaces the entire prior limits record. Adding maxDepth can discard maxAdmittedTargets and maxCandidateReadAttempts; once mode accepts that configuration.
misuse: A host tunes depth and unintentionally removes its remote-source read/admission budgets. The public probe observes one admitted vertex before tuning and three afterward.
proposal: Preserve the documented replacement policy but make it explicit through replaceLimits or a replaceLimits() operation. If choosing field-wise merging instead, specify explicit per-bound clearing and keep atomic validation.
tradeoff: The explicit replacement name is a mechanical API migration. Field-wise merging would be an additional behavior change and requires migrating callers that intentionally clear bounds.

title: sortChildrenHints actually transforms expansion membership
counterpart: ChildHintSorter versus REWRITE_CHILD_HINTS
behavior: The callback result becomes the new expansion list without a permutation check. It can remove, duplicate or invent hints, not only sort them.
misuse: An apparently ordering-only customization silently substitutes a different discovered child; the probe replaces a with replacement.
proposal: Use transformChildHints / ChildHintTransformer and the async counterpart, including inspection operation vocabulary. Standardize childHints in related accessor names during this migration.
tradeoff: Breaking option/type renames preserve current capability. A comparator-only sorter is a separate possible restriction and must not be imposed silently.
fable: F13 discusses naming stem; transformer behavior considered separately

title: Current reference confuses rejected forms with supported policy
counterpart: Source result tags and configurable object options versus callback observations
behavior: The prerequisite paragraph advertises undefined and { vertexContent: null } normalization, which runtime rejects. The rewrite paragraph at line 1162 advertises isComposite/getKeyPath as options, although they are bound context observations.
misuse: A client copies an advertised adapter return or sets isComposite and receives TypeError; TypeScript also contradicts the guide.
proposal: Document tagged missing/omitted results and supported isArray/isObject options. Identify isComposite and getKeyPath as callback/binder observations. Keep the existing strict runtime.
tradeoff: Repair the guide and migrate integrations written against the stale prose; no compatibility restoration or runtime change is needed.
fable: considered in owner appendix; not ranked

title: omittedWorkDependencies means an absent list, not an omitted vertex
counterpart: DagVertexOmitted, omittedIds, omission slots and replaceOmissions
behavior: This policy applies when a found vertex omits its dependsOnWork declaration. Explicit lists, including [], override it. It does not change deliberate vertex omission or W/C satisfaction.
misuse: A host mistakes none for a policy about omitted prerequisites and leaves live vertices with unintentionally independent work.
proposal: Rename the key to dependsOnWorkDefault: none | discoveryParentWork across configuration, patches and preparation inputs.
tradeoff: Mechanical breaking key rename; preserve explicit-list precedence, synthetic-entry behavior and acknowledged omission semantics. Severity reflects potential scheduling mistakes, not a current scheduler defect.

title: PreparedDag.vertices hides its lossy projection
counterpart: PreparedDag.definition.vertices and DagSummary.vertices
behavior: PreparedDag.vertices contains live-vertex descriptions with live children only. Omission slots, omittedIds and ordered entry information belong to definition.
misuse: A host persists the convenient vertices projection as revision topology and loses omitted prerequisite identities or root-slot order.
proposal: Rename the projection to liveVertexSummaries, or remove it in favor of a named summarization helper. Keep definition as the faithful reconstruction contract.
tradeoff: Mechanical property rename. Existing documentation already warns against round trips, so this is rated 2/5 rather than Fable’s 3/5.

title: isTraversalLeaf measures expansion policy, not resolved children
counterpart: VertexView.hasNoChildHints() and ResolvedTreeView.getChildrenOf()
behavior: The predicate is skipped expansion OR no hints. A root with all hints omitted has no resolved children yet returns false; a root skipped after its first child retains that child yet returns true. Async uses the same rule.
misuse: A post-traversal leaf collector misses structural leaves and includes retained internal vertices.
proposal: Remove the convenience or split it into isChildExpansionSkipped and the existing hint/structural queries. If retaining the exact boolean, name it hasNoChildHintsOrSkippedExpansion.
tradeoff: Callers must choose which predicate they intended. A new isResolvedLeaf would additionally need an explicit policy for incomplete discovery.
fable: related surface asymmetry in F17; behavior not ranked

title: Work-session creation and wrapping share the same verb
counterpart: createDagWorkSession(runner) versus preparedDag.createWorkSession()
behavior: Free factories wrap an existing runner. Two wrappers share progress but issue mutually foreign tickets. Prepared-DAG factories allocate independent runner progress.
misuse: A coordinator creates two wrappers expecting isolated executions; one wrapper’s settlement changes the other’s progress.
proposal: Use bindDagWorkSession / bindAsyncDagWorkSession for existing-runner wrappers; retain createWorkSession for independent creation.
tradeoff: Rename only; preserve shared progress, session-local tickets, single-owner execution and duplicate-settlement behavior.

title: Rewrite output collapses deleted roots and null documents
counterpart: outputAtReturn versus FINISHED-only getOutput(), and root presence
behavior: A deleted root and a retained root whose value is null both become null before conversion. The existing time distinction between the two output APIs does not recover presence.
misuse: A document host treats null as deletion and cannot distinguish an intentionally null document without inspecting runner topology.
proposal: Expose getOutputResult(): { kind: present; value: Out } | { kind: absent }, plus a corresponding captured result or explicit presence in converter context.
tradeoff: An additive route can preserve current getters. Specify whether absence invokes conversion, and retain completion gating and existing conversion behavior.
fable: considered in owner appendix; not ranked

title: Cycle payload vertexIds names two different kinds of evidence
counterpart: discoveryCycle/DagDiscoveryCycleError witnesses versus structuralCycle SCC membership
behavior: Discovery cycles expose an ordered closed witness; structural cycles expose component membership. The shared vertexIds field does not identify that difference.
misuse: A formatter joins consecutive IDs with arrows for every issue and invents edges for an SCC.
proposal: Use cycleWitnessVertexIds for ordered witnesses and componentVertexIds for SCC evidence. Keep dependencyCycleComponents, whose name is already accurate.
tradeoff: Breaking diagnostic-field migration; preserve actual ordering, repeated closing identity and arbitrary ID identity.

title: Omission identity has two incompatible presence encodings
counterpart: Source/resolved omission vertexId versus DagDefinitionSlot.identity
behavior: Source and resolved omissions distinguish anonymous versus known identity by own-property presence; definitions use identity: { vertexId } | null. A real ID may be undefined.
misuse: A converter testing slot.vertexId !== undefined turns a known-undefined omission into an anonymous one and changes prerequisite identity.
proposal: Use the explicit identity wrapper consistently for omission-bearing records. Keep satisfiesDependencies: true as the separate discovery acknowledgment.
tradeoff: Breaking record migration with an extra wrapper; convert existing records using own-property checks, not truthiness. Do not promise arbitrary IDs survive JSON serialization.

title: Stall dependency records use id/unmet instead of canonical DAG names
counterpart: DagMilestone.vertexId, DagVertexProgress and DagDeferredWork
behavior: Stall diagnostics expose dependencies: { id, unmet }[] while neighboring DAG records use vertexId and explicit prerequisite names. Diagnostic arrays are detached copies and are currently mutable.
misuse: A formatter reuses canonical vertexId access and silently omits the stalled vertex from these records.
proposal: Use vertexId and unmetPrerequisiteIds in dependency records. Consider readonly owned diagnostic collections as a separate type-design choice; detached mutation is not a current engine-state leak.
tradeoff: Breaking formatter-field migration. Preserve waiter/prerequisite direction and the distinction between W/C constraint edges and summary ID lists.

title: Work-session inspection erases its known DAG type
counterpart: DagTraversalRunner.inspect() and TreeDagExecutionInspection
behavior: The session base extends unspecialized TraversalExecutionState although inspect delegates to a DAG runner. session.inspect().chains fails typechecking despite being present.
misuse: A coordinator retains a second runner reference or casts inspection just to read pending chains or requests.
proposal: Specialize session control to TraversalExecutionState<TreeDagExecutionInspection<DagVisitorPhase>>. An exported DagWorkSessionControl capability could also name the shared sync/async control surface.
tradeoff: Runtime behavior is unchanged; structural mocks need richer records. Keep general execution defaults family-neutral for walkers.

title: Public walking link types discard hydration policy
counterpart: GraphWalkTarget/GraphWalkLink versus resolver and inlineOrCached source branches
behavior: The broad exported target/link unions cannot express a particular hydration mode, although source unions enforce it. A helper returning GraphWalkLink[] cannot plug into an inlineOrCached source merely because its implementation emits inline targets.
misuse: An adapter author widens a helper to the public alias and then needs manual Extract/indexed-access types or assertions to reuse it.
proposal: Parameterize public target/link types by hydration mode with the broad union as default, or export explicit ResolverGraphWalkTarget and InlineOrCachedGraphWalkTarget/link aliases.
tradeoff: Additive typing improves composition without weakening invalid-mode rejection or first-admitted-resolution rules; additional aliases cost surface area.
fable: considered in owner appendix; not ranked

title: Readonly discovery hints are rejected at input boundaries
counterpart: Readonly dependency/definition inputs and observation collections
behavior: VertexContentInput.$childHints and REWRITE_CHILD_HINTS.newHints require mutable arrays. Reusable as-const descriptions fail assignment.
misuse: A source author copies or asserts an immutable hint tuple solely to satisfy the API’s input type.
proposal: Accept readonly hints in source/command inputs; copy into owned mutable storage at the relevant boundary and keep editable standalone outputs mutable.
tradeoff: Input types broaden, but constructor aliasing must be specified explicitly. Existing standalone construction currently retains the supplied array; this proposal does not claim otherwise.
fable: considered in owner appendix; not ranked

title: Walking source names both the adapter and an edge endpoint
counterpart: GraphWalkOptions.source versus edge-event and follow-context source
behavior: The option is a GraphWalkSource adapter; edge event/context source is a GraphWalkVertex. Current reference explicitly warns about the distinction.
misuse: An adapter integration shadows its source variable in a callback or looks for outgoing on event.source.
proposal: Use fromVertex on edge events and follow context, matching edge.from. Keep source for the adapter and retain the tagged target resolution wrapper.
tradeoff: Mechanical callback-field migration. A symmetric name must not erase the target’s found/omitted distinction.

title: Throwing graph/tree queries look like nullable sibling queries
counterpart: getChildrenOf/getParentsOf/getVisitStageOf versus getVertexId/getPathsTo and tree getPathTo
behavior: Unknown handles yield null from several queries but throw Error from identity/path queries. A public probe verifies both behaviors on the same foreign handle.
misuse: After a cascade deletion, a host tolerates absent children then calls getPathsTo on the stale handle and unexpectedly throws.
proposal: Make strict lookups explicit, for example requireVertexId and requirePathsTo/requirePathTo, or offer clearly named nonthrowing variants with tagged identity presence.
tradeoff: Rename-only strict methods preserve behavior. Never use null/undefined as an absent-ID sentinel: both are valid IDs. A new tagged tryGetVertexId avoids that collision.

title: Milestone explanations use unknown where endpoint status uses unresolved
counterpart: DagExplanation.kind versus DagMilestoneStatus.kind within explanation/blocker results
behavior: An absent captured identity is unknown in a top-level explanation and unresolved in an endpoint status. A known explanation may correctly represent an omitted identity with null progress.
misuse: A diagnostic UI maintains two labels for the same absent-identity fact or mistakenly treats known as synonymous with live.
proposal: Choose one absent-identity literal across those layers; optionally expose explicit live/omitted identity status in known results. Preserve the valid distinction between known and live.
tradeoff: Literal/union migration for a modest clarity gain. Current nullable progress is typed correctly; this is not a correctness defect and is rated below Fable’s 2/5.

title: Fragment instantiation suggests an invariant its result does not enforce
counterpart: DagFragmentInstance versus DagFragment and nominal DagWorkTicket
behavior: DagFragmentInstance is exactly DagFragment. instantiateDagFragment maps IDs, and composition accepts a fragment without that mapping step; it establishes no distinct instance capability.
misuse: A caller assumes an instance is automatically namespaced or provenance-checked, then composes colliding IDs.
proposal: Use mapDagFragmentIds returning DagFragment and remove the redundant instance alias. Keep mapping explicit; do not add nominal restrictions unless composition actually needs them.
tradeoff: Mechanical renames preserve existing behavior. mapId already exposes the real policy, limiting the practical impact.

title: VertexRef has different editing authority in public and internal declarations
counterpart: Public VertexHandle-as-VertexRef alias versus internal MutableRef<Vertex> alias
behavior: Supported VertexRef imports are safe handles. A reachable internal alias with the same short name is mutable, so declaration navigation shows identical names with different authority.
misuse: A reader assumes setValue is available on an observed ref after following a mutable internal declaration.
proposal: Use VertexHandle as the sole public name and InternalVertexRef or MutableVertexRef internally. Simplify public mapped declarations where doing so improves hovers.
tradeoff: Type import migration only. There is no mutable runner-handle leak, so compatibility value may outweigh this optional cleanup.
